question: If a copper wire is moving through a uniform magnetic field, then the direction of the induced current can be found using the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fleming's right-hand rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Using Fleming's right-hand rule, we may determine the direction of current produced in a wire travelling in a magnetic field.**
 
• The **rule states that if we extend our right hand's forefinger, middle finger, and thumb perpendicular to one another as shown in the figure, with the thumb pointing toward the conductor's motion and the forefinger pointing toward the direction of the magnetic field, the middle finger will give us the direction of the flow of induced current in the circuit**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfcd3cefffb0fffdda3b6c44030e60dd8a3e663dc8dd6f11f6d9b0734f66e57a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maxwell's right-hand screw rule**

 
 
• **​**According to **Maxwell's screw rule, the magnetic field's direction can be determined by rotating a right-handed screw so that it advances in the same direction as the regular current.** The Maxwell corkscrew rule is another name for the right-hand thumb rule.
 
 
 
• **Maxwell's left-hand screw rule**
 
 
• **​**It is used to establish the** direction of the magnetic field encircling a conductor that is capable of carrying straight current.** If the direction of the magnetic field lines connected to the current-carrying conductor is known, it can be utilised to calculate the direction of the electric current in that conductor.
 
 
 
• **Fleming's left-hand rule**
 
 
• **​****To identify the direction of force acting on a current-carrying wire positioned in a magnetic field, utilise Fleming's left-hand rule. The thumb indicates the direction of force acting on the wire if the thumb, index finger (along the magnetic field), and middle finger (along the current) are kept mutually perpendicular.**
